references.text: The parable of the lost sheep has a corresponding structure: the one who finds the lost calls friends and neighbors together to share the joy. [ref:Luk 15:6|Luke 15:6] uses almost identical wording – "Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost" – which underscores the parallel between the two parables about what was lost.

Jesus explains that there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents ([ref:Luk 15:7|Luke 15:7]). The joy among the women friends and neighbors in verse 9 reflects this heavenly joy, which is further explained in verse 10.

The verse that follows immediately ([ref:Luk 15:10|Luke 15:10]) gives the theological application of the parable: "In the same way, I tell you, there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents." The woman's joy over the found drachma points forward to the angels' joy.

In the parable of the prodigal son, the reunion is celebrated with a feast and joy ([ref:Luk 15:23-24|Luke 15:23-24]). The same motif – gathering others to share the joy that what was lost has been found – runs through all three parables in Luke 15.

The older brother is told that it is right to rejoice because "your brother was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found" ([ref:Luk 15:32|Luke 15:32]). The call to rejoice together (Συγχάρητέ μοι) in verse 9 finds its parallel here.

Zephaniah prophesies that the Lord will rejoice over his people with gladness ([ref:Sef 3:17|Zephaniah 3:17]). God's own joy in "finding again" his people provides an Old Testament background for the joy in the parable of the lost coin.

Isaiah describes how God rejoices over his people as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride ([ref:Jes 62:5|Isaiah 62:5]). This divine joy over restoration is reflected in the woman's joy over the found coin.

The Lord promises to seek out the lost, bring back the exiled, and bind up the injured ([ref:Esek 34:16|Ezekiel 34:16]). God's active search for what was lost parallels the woman's diligent search for the drachma.

Jesus summarizes his mission: "The Son of Man came to seek and save the lost" ([ref:Luk 19:10|Luke 19:10]). The woman who diligently searches for the lost coin illustrates precisely this aspect of Jesus' ministry.

Paul urges the Philippians: "Rejoice in the Lord always!" ([ref:Fil 4:4|Philippians 4:4]). The shared joy that the woman invites others to share reflects the community's joy in the Lord when what was lost has been found.
